text:
mike: ran an Nsight Systems capture on the failing Dedicated job this morning. attaching the quick notes below — looks like a repeating pattern every ~120ms where a memcpy on a low-priority stream wakes a GPU and we see a 10-30ms kernel start gap on the main inference stream.

mike: capture: `gpu:0 timeline 0-6s`, heatmap shows stacked memcpy bursts at 0.12s, 0.24s, 0.36s... main compute kernels (attention/ffn) start delayed right after each burst.

tara: can you paste the timeline snippet? small screenshot is fine.

mike: pasted ASCII timeline (super reduced):
```
0.120s: memcpy_h2d S=stream7 size=3.2MB
0.122s: kernel_attn S=stream0 queued
0.125s: kernel_attn S=stream0 start (delayed)
0.240s: memcpy_h2d S=stream7 size=2.9MB
0.243s: kernel_ffn S=stream0 queued
0.247s: kernel_ffn S=stream0 start (delayed)
```

mike: note the ~3-5ms extra queue->start latency after memcpy bursts. nvprof/insights show stream7 is doing async copies from pinned pool.

raj: that sounds like host thread preemption/wakeup jitter — CPU woke the H2D copy thread which contended with the main caller that submits kernels. any `nvidia-smi topo` for CPU affinity?

mike: submission is from thread pool worker pinned to CPU 3 but the pinned-copy helper is running on CPU 12. We saw several `sched_wakeup` spikes in perf during the bursts.

lena: could be batching heuristic: small microbatches trigger prefix cache prefetch which does a copy for keys into a staging buffer on stream7. If prefetch aligns with main submits, we lose launch ordering.

tara: hypothesis: copy on low-prio stream is forcing a GPU power-state or creating PCIe activity that stalls kernel launch scheduling for the high-prio stream. Did Nsight show stream priorities?

mike: yes, stream0 is high priority (priority 0), stream7 is default priority (priority 0 as well in current build). No priority differentiation.

raj: two actionable items: 1) try elevating copy stream to a lower (higher numeric) priority so compute keeps precedence; 2) coalesce prefetches to avoid many small memcpys.

mike: quick test: changed copy to use cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(stream7, cudaStreamNonBlocking, -1) -> made it higher priority than default. result: the kernel start gaps disappeared but CPU jitter increased because copy thread now influences CPU scheduling more.

lena: that's expected — priority moves scheduling pressure to submitters. not ideal. We want copy to use an async copy engine path that doesn't compete with kernel dispatch. Consider pinned-buffer pooling + batched H2D using a single large staging transfer per inference tick.

tara: what about making copy stream non-blocking but lower priority (positive numeric)? can test with +1. Also check if using `cuMemcpyAsync` on same stream as compute but with `cudaMemcpyKind::DeviceToDevice` helps (if using UVA/GPUDirect we might avoid CPU wakeups).

mike: ran +1 (lower priority) experiment: memcpy still caused short wakeups but now kernel launch latencies dropped by ~60% in the heatmap. overall p50 latency improved 8%, p99 unchanged.

raj: p99 unchanged suggests outliers are still CPU preemptions or intermittent large copies. Do we have trace slices where p99 aligns with a longer memcpy (e.g., >10MB)?

mike: yes, one of the long tails correlated to a 28MB copy triggered by cache miss during rare prefix expansion. that one also coincided with a context switch on the submission thread (`sched_switch` from mike-thread -> unrelated-daemon).

lena: action: add metrics to the batcher to emit `prefetch_size_bytes` per request and count of prefetches per tick so we can correlate spikes in telemetry with traces.

tara: for short-term mitigation, let's: 1) make copy stream lower priority (+1), 2) aggregate small prefetches into a single copy when total < 64KB threshold, 3) add a jittered submission backoff when memory pool is under high pressure.

raj: long-term: refactor prefetch to use device-side async copy (if hardware supports) or a dedicated pinned-thread with real-time affinity; also consider launching kernel dispatch from a separate, affinity-stable thread to reduce interruption.

mike: I'll run a 12-hour perf run with the +1 change and the batched prefetch threshold set to 64KB. posting results tomorrow. tagging @perf-bot to kick off the nightly capture. :rocket:

perf-bot: scheduled nightly-capture for job-id=dedicated-prod-42 at 02:00 UTC, attached trace will be archived to /traces/dedicated-prod-42/2026-03-18/

mike: thanks — next steps tracked in JIRA #INF-821, I'll paste the link when the run completes.

lena: nice work, keeping the heatmap approach for follow-up. :thumbsup:
